The history readouts (objects4d, retention, accept history) read session_X/timeline.pkl, whose scenes are RENDERED at each snapshot time (game.py snapshot()/_render_scene: the scene list stores renders, not rows), so a row pruned later is still in every earlier snapshot. The decided version 29d7f6e (prune deleting) passed the accept history check on real A->B->C and synthetic A->B. What P1 did change: the official tsdf export of session B renders A's stored keyframes at their times, so pruned A rows were still rendered there; without P1 those renders use the pruned model (= the decided version's readout, real B 92.42 / synthetic B 87.76).

Crashed run syn_row4i B (P1 on): 13.2 GB used at frame 2269 with ~3.0 M alive rows plus the P1-ended rows (real B had 711,299 = 28 % of the model; synthetic B not counted before the crash), failed at frame 3241 (3.11 M alive) with dmesg dxgkio_make_resident ENOMEM. Decided version (no P1), same synthetic B: 2.96 -> 3.16 M alive rows, ran to the end on this card; older no-P1 synthetic runs sampled by nvidia-smi peaked at 11.4 GB used (syn_row4v6.log.vram). The readout in the log will give the actual per-round peak (this is also the first direct measurement; earlier numbers are nvidia-smi samples).

On metric failure: offline analysis on checkpoint_b (closure_compare, state_rows, g1_decompose) only.

What remains unmeasured: P1 rows (opacity below GaME's prune threshold raw < 0.1) stayed rendered, frozen, for this session's earlier keyframes during later training iterations; removing them changes those renders by rows the published method deletes.

Direct measurement replaces the estimate (scratch gpu_steady.py on syn_row4i checkpoint_a restored exactly as --resume does): 2,966,470 rows, 4.22 GB allocated, 100 % accounted, 1421 B/row - of which the I1 label table 1.768 GB (596 B/row: dense N x 149 float32 for the synthetic labels; real has 18 labels = 72 B/row), f_rest param+Adam 1.60 GB (540 B/row), the rest 0.85 GB. Keyframes live on the CPU (0 GB). The earlier '977 B/row + 6.4 GB fixed' was wrong: there is no large fixed part; the table scaled with rows and labels. The unexplained ~2.7 GB of the crash: (i) the label table itself (not in the 977 B/row), (ii) the rasterizer's used_count buffer (obj_num+1) x N float32 = 1.8 GB transient at every vote render on the synthetic map, (iii) the densify/prune copies: FlashSplat replaces each param group by indexing/cat (old and new coexist per group: f_rest group 1.6 GB -> +0.5 GB transient) and our per-row columns including the label table (+1.77 GB transient) - both crashes' tracebacks are in that label-table copy (10-07 v5: torch.cat in densification_postfix at 12.0 -> 15.8 GB used; 10-09 syn_row4i: label_weight[keep] in prune); (iv) allocator cache (expandable segments; reserved > allocated). The 10-07 v5 run (code 82558fe, NO P1, 3.44 M rows) died the same way, so P1 was not the only cause - it raised the row count (28-42 % ended rows kept) on top of the table.

I1 label table stored sparse on the GPU (LabelTable, update_layer/backends/game/label_table.py): non-zero entries only (1.75 per row synthetic, 1.86 real): 104 MB instead of 1.77 GB on the synthetic map, and the densify/prune copies shrink accordingly. Same values: sums formed from the same two operands, best label = first column of the largest entry (dense torch.max rule), rows without entries -> (0, 0). Verified offline on the REAL checkpoint tables (synthetic A 2.97 M x 149, real B 2.58 M x 18), every operation the backend uses bitwise equal to the dense path: roundtrip, max values and indices (ties, 3,045 / 7,181 empty rows), += render-shaped delta, rows[keep], rows[par] with duplicate parents, append rows/columns, CSR checkpoint roundtrip (records/label_table_check_20261009.py; 13/13 PASS on both). CPU unit test added (18/18 tests pass on the snapshot). Checkpoint format unchanged (CSR), so syn_row4i/checkpoint_a loads unchanged. Not a model change: no decision, threshold or value changes.

GPU_GUARD_GB default 13.5 (run.py) and in queue81.sh; it reads max_memory_reserved (what the driver holds), allocated printed next to it. New prediction for synthetic B: restored state 2.55 GB (4.22 - 1.77 + 0.10) + B's rows; training/render buffers and the 1.8 GB used_count transient on top: expected peak reserved 7-10 GB; the densify/prune transient no longer carries the 1.77 GB table.

Stated explicitly: this synthetic B run IS the synthetic AB validation of the memory fix (no synthetic B checkpoint exists under the new rules to test offline; A's checkpoint is reused since A has no earlier-session rows and the table values are unchanged). Guard trip or driver error = stop, no retry, no rerun; metric stop rules as in the main review.
